llm.summary: The stagflation cocktail is back on with force: the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.444%, the highest since 2004, the 5-year breached 5% for the first time since 2007, Brent-linked crude printed $107, the dollar hit a two-month high and 30-year mortgage rates broke 7%. That is a complete reversal of yesterday's post-Fed relief rally — the 'Fed regains trust' narrative lasted exactly one session, and Philadelphia Fed's Paulson signalling 'modest' further moves means the market is now pricing hikes, not cuts. Equities slipped broadly with small caps and gold miners hit hardest, gold itself fell to ~$4,267 as real yields and the dollar squeezed it, and dividend/duration proxies (REITs, utilities, staples) are the worst rotation reads in the dataset. Inside AI, two genuinely new cracks appeared: Oracle filed a force majeure notice on a data-center project (-4%), and Apple claimed new Macs beat cloud AI on cost per token, which pressured NVDA — the first credible challenges to the 'infinite capex, infinite margin' framing, even as AWS and NVIDIA committed to 2 million more GPUs. Michael Burry doubled his shorts on Micron and Palantir on an AI chip price-collapse thesis, days before MU reports. Macro-politically, Trump and Xi extended the trade truce three months to January 10 with rare earths still China's leverage — a de-escalation that removes a tail risk without solving anything. For the book, the ~15% energy sleeve is now the right sleeve at the right time and yesterday's instinct to trim it was wrong; the live risks are Realty Income against a 5.44% long bond, the capital-markets complex (GS, SCHW) as Piper/Houlihan/Blackstone/Lazard/TPG all sold off, and consumer credit exposure via AXP as 7% mortgages and rising auto loan rates bite. The regime model's drift toward Contraction (28.4%, +9.3) with Reflation collapsing (-9.8) says this is a cost-of-capital shock inside a slowdown, not a growth boom.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: risk-off driven by the cost of money, not by earnings. With the 30-year at a 20-year high, the 5-year above 5% and crude at $107, the discount rate and the input cost are rising simultaneously — that is the textbook equity de-rating combination and it is showing up exactly where it should: small caps, gold miners, REITs, asset managers, brokers, homebuilding-adjacent retail. Expect continued leadership from energy (rotation +69) and from banks with liability-side advantage, and continued punishment of anything whose valuation is a duration bet. Gold is not working as the hedge here because the dollar and real yields are the transmission mechanism; cash and short energy-linked cash flows are. The two-day whipsaw (Tuesday's relief, Wednesday's rout) tells you positioning is unstable and conviction is thin — treat rallies as tactical until the long bond stops making new highs.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: sticky-inflation slowdown where the AI capex cycle collides with physical and financial constraints. Oracle's force majeure is the template — the binding constraints on AI buildout are power interconnection, permits, transformers and construction labour, not chips, so timelines slip and the capex that does happen disproportionately pays electricians, turbine makers, pipeline operators and utilities rather than software. Simultaneously, Apple's cost-per-token claim and the edge-AI attention surge open the first real debate about whether inference economics migrate off cloud, which caps the terminal-value story for centralized GPU rental even if it does nothing to near-term orders. Earnings breadth stays narrow: AI infrastructure survivors, energy, and banks; the trading-down consumer (Costco, value retail) keeps winning while Darden, MGM, housing and discretionary travel deteriorate. A 7% mortgage plus 5%+ auto and card funding costs will show up in credit metrics by Q4 — that is the path from Stagflation to Contraction in the regime model.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: a 5% risk-free rate is the regime, not the anomaly, and capital permanently migrates from narrative-priced asset-light businesses to physical chokepoints — electrons, molecules, memory, optics, copper, pipelines, skilled trades. Three structural stamps from today: (1) energy security is now a financial variable, with $107 crude, a proposed diesel export ban, and Mitsui buying LNG specifically to feed data centers — energy and compute are becoming the same asset class; (2) global debt at $365 trillion means governments compete with corporates for capital at every auction, so term premium stays elevated and levered business models stay impaired; (3) China's rare-earth leverage at the summit confirms that supply-chain sovereignty, not tariffs, is the long war — reshoring capex and domestic materials processing remain multi-decade spends even when industrial flows are negative today. Businesses whose moat was cheap capital (marginal housing, levered consumer, second-tier AI capex, REIT roll-ups) stay structurally disadvantaged for years.

short_term: Housing demand is being rationed by payment, not price: 7% mortgages freeze both moves and refis, pushing households toward repair-and-stay-put behaviour — supportive for maintenance/MRO spend (HD attention +51% and flagged not-priced) but destructive for turnover-linked consumption.

Consumers are trading down and trading out of discretionary experiences: Darden's Olive Garden slowdown, MGM's collapsed takeover, and the Consumer Discretionary rotation at -73 all say the mid-tier experience economy is losing wallet share to value retail and to essentials.

Rising car loan rates are converting auto demand into a financing decision; Hyundai out-selling Ford on hybrids shows buyers optimizing total cost of ownership (fuel at $107 crude plus rate) rather than brand.

Investors are demanding yield without duration: they are dumping long Treasuries, dividend stocks and gold miners while family offices (per Citi) add equities and private equity — a barbell of inflation-protected cash flow and illiquid optionality.

Younger investors are institutionalizing: the Gen Z shift from sports betting to ETFs, plus New York's suit against Polymarket, marks a re-channeling of speculative energy into regulated wrappers — structurally good for brokers and asset gatherers even as capital-markets fees wobble.

Enterprises are buying security preemptively because AI agents are now attackers: OpenAI's agent autonomously hacking an Australian government site and Island's $6.4B valuation show budget moving from optional to mandatory.
long_term: People will increasingly want AI that runs locally for cost, latency and privacy reasons — Apple's cost-per-token claim plus the edge-AI query surge ('ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service') signals inference migrating toward devices, changing who captures the compute margin.

Health is being re-framed as a procedure-and-device consumption decision: the 107% surge in robotic-surgery queries spanning hysterectomy, hernia, prostate and knee replacement is an aging population actively shopping for less-invasive interventions, and the dataset flags it as unpriced.

Delegation replaces search: Meta's Muse agent, the human-concierge test, and the $1,299 glasses point to consumers paying for an intermediary that does things rather than shows things — the largest re-plumbing of advertising economics since mobile.

Energy is becoming a status and security good, not a commodity line item: district heating investment, LNG contracting for data centers, pipeline races and grid-failure searches all reflect a population and a corporate sector paying up for guaranteed electrons.

Physical labour with digital leverage gets scarce and expensive: electricians, HVAC, pipeline and fab construction workers are the real bottleneck to AI, reshoring and grid capex — wage premia persist and sustain contractor margins.

Households are being forced into multigenerational financial management — the MarketWatch cluster on aging parents, estate plans, scams and Social Security overpayments reflects a demographic-scale need for advice, custody and fraud protection that scaled wealth platforms will monetize.
